findings.finding: The plan's mechanism for moving the roster into the system prompt is under-specified and likely inconsistent with how _resolve_system works. _resolve_system(prompt_id, plan, cfg) renders only a {{plan}} template variable; the roster is a runtime-computed string that differs per review and cannot be embedded in a static prompt file, so it cannot be 'byte-stable inside the cached prefix' without either (a) extending _resolve_system's signature to accept and render a {{roster}} variable, or (b) appending the roster to the system_prompt string after _resolve_system returns. Neither is described in the Scope entry for passes.py, and option (b) would make the system prompt non-byte-stable (defeating the caching benefit the plan claims).
findings.location: Approach section (defect 2, roster caching rationale); Scope: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact mechanism by which the sibling roster enters the system prompt: name which function signature changes (e.g., `_resolve_system` gains a `roster: str = ''` parameter, or `pass1_container` appends the roster to the resolved system string), and confirm this placement is byte-stable across pairings.

findings.finding: The plan says to move the sibling roster into the system prompt ('beside the parent plan, which _resolve_system keeps byte-stable inside the cached prefix'), but _resolve_system(prompt_id, plan, cfg) has no parameter for roster content and assembles the system prompt entirely from the prompt-library template. scenarios: An implementer reading the plan cannot determine whether to (a) add a roster parameter to _resolve_system, (b) append the roster string after calling _resolve_system, (c) add {{roster}} as a template variable to plan_review_container.md, or (d) restructure pass1_container to build the system prompt differently — each choice has different caching implications.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify that the warm-then-fan-out gate (`CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` in `pass1.py`) is still cleared — or explicitly adjusted — after the roster moves into the system prompt, so the stated linear-vs-quadratic cost guarantee holds for the target parent population.
evidence: Plan claims: 'the roster is written once and read thereafter' and 'roster cost linear, not quadratic, in child count'
pass1.py:187: `warm = parent_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and len(pairings) >= 2` — warming only fires when parent prefix alone exceeds 4096 tokens

The roster (now carrying each child's full AC text) is added to the system prompt, but the warm gate checks `parent_tokens` (the plan's token count), not the combined system-prompt token count — if the plan text alone is below 4096 tokens, the roster addition does not help clear the floor
No token-budget or cache-floor analysis for the enriched system prompt is provided in the plan
findings.finding: The plan asserts that moving the sibling roster into the system prompt makes roster cost 'linear, not quadratic, in child count' via Anthropic prefix caching, but does not verify whether the expanded system prompt (plan + full child AC corpus) consistently clears the CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096 floor that gates the warm-then-fan-out optimization — leaving the cost-linearity claim unresolved for small or medium parents whose plan text alone may not reach that floor.
findings.location: Approach section (2), 'Move it into the system prompt beside the parent plan'; also pass1.py:187 (CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS gate)
scenarios: A parent with a concise plan (<4096 tokens) gets no warm prefix even after the roster is moved to system prompt — each pairing misses the cache, defeating the stated linear-cost goal
A parent with many children each carrying long AC sections pushes the system prompt well above the floor — the caching benefit is real for this case but the plan conflates it with the general case
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note in the plan (and a corresponding test assertion) confirming that `_run_container` measures the combined system-prompt token count (plan + roster) against `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, or update the gate condition accordingly — e.g. `parent_tokens + roster_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`.

findings.finding: The plan lists plan_review_G3.md as a Scope file to update (instruct the reviewer to test absence against roster AC items), but does NOT list plan_review_container.md. The container prompt (plan_review_container.md) currently drives the actual absence-checking instruction ('when you flag an ABSENCE... CHECK it against the WHOLE roster first; only flag it if NO sibling covers it'). G3's rubric is the criterion-level spec, but the container prompt is the LLM's operative instruction — if plan_review_container.md is not updated to tell the model how to use the richer roster (now carrying AC text, not just id+title), the behavioral change the plan intends will not land.
scenarios: An implementer updates G3.md to reference roster AC items but leaves plan_review_container.md unchanged. The LLM receives both the updated G3 rubric text and the unchanged container-prompt instruction. The container prompt's instruction ('check against the roster') does not tell the model to read AC items — the behavioral gap persists despite the G3 rubric change.
